 JUDGMENT
The petitioner has filed this claim petition U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act, 1989, against respondents seeking compensation on account of injuries sustained by him in Motor Vehicle Accident.

02. The brief facts of the case of the petitioner is as under:
On 28.03.2024 at about 03.15 p.m, when the petitioner was going in his Honda Motor Cycle Dio (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.3669/2024 bearing No.KA-06-EY-1658 as a rider from his house from Gedhlahalli towards Kunigal Junction, in front of Uthsava Kalyana Mantapa, Ring Road, at that time suddenly a driver was driving the Toyota Itios Car bearing No.KA-06-D-9673, came from back side, in rash and negligent manner, with high speed and dashed against the petitioner's vehicle.

Due to impact,
the petitioner fell down along with the Motor Cycle and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident he was shifted to Government District hospital,
Tumakuru, for treatment, wherein he was treated as an inpatient from 28.03.2024 to 31.03.2024 and after the accident the petitioner is taking treatment and psychotherapy on regular basis in Vinayaka hospital, Tumakuru and Sreyas hosptial,
Tumakuru which is incurring his additional expenditure which has reached few lakhs as on today.

Prior to accident the petitioner was hale and healthy and was aged about 42 years and working as licenced Surveyor in Chikkanayakanahalli Taluk and was earning Rs.50,000/- p.m and he has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards hospitalization,
transportation and for medicines and nourishment.

The petitioner is unable to continue his job as before and he has lost his job, which is due to injuries and disability caused (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.3669/2024 due to said accident, which resulted the petitioner to undergo severe mental stress and agony and presently the petitioner is without employment.

The accident occurred due to rash and negligent manner driving by the driver of Toyota Itios Car and in this regard the Tumakuru Traffic Police have registered a case against driver of the said offending vehicle.

Hence, the respondent No.1 being the insurer and respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with cost and interest.
03.
Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.2 remained absent and hence, was placed exparte.
On service of notice, the respondent No.1 has appeared before the tribunal and has filed written statement.

04. Respondent No.1 in its objections has denied the entire case of the petitioner and further denied alleged accident, negligence of the driver of offending Car, age, avocation, income of the petitioner,

2 nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner, treatment taken by the petitioner and expenses incurred by the petitioner and contended that the driver of Car was not at all responsible for the cause of accident and the rider/petitioner of scooter, has rode the same at a high speed, in rash and negligent (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.3669/2024 manner, tried to overtake an another vehicle, but he could not do, due to other vehicles are coming from opposite direction and he applied sudden brake to his scooter and hence this accident has taken place and the driver of Etios Car was not holding any valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident and the car was not having valid RC,
FC, Permit, Insurance etc., to ply in place of accident and as on the date of accident and therefore,
has contravened the provisions of M.V. Act and has committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy by the owner.

05. Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following Issues have been framed by my learned predecessor: -
ISSUES 01.

Whether the petitioner proves that he was sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 28.03.2024 at about 3.15 p.m, in front of Utsava Kalyana Mantapa, from Gedhlahalli towards Kunigal Junction, Ring Road Tumakuru, due to rash and negligent driving of Toyota Etios Car bearing registration No.KA-06-D-9673 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
03. What Order or Award?
06. In order to prove the case, the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and got examined MRO as PW.2 and got marked 18 documents as Ex.P.1 to 18 and closed his side evidence.

07. By way of rebuttal, the counsel for the respondent No.1 submits no oral evidence, hence,
respondent No.1 evidence is taken as nil and closed its side evidence.
08. Heard both sides.
The counsel for the respondent No.1 has filed written arguments.

09. My findings on the aforesaid issues are as under:-
 Issue No.1 In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3

As per final order  for the following:

3  REASONS 10. Issue No.1:- The petitioner in order to prove his case, he himself examined as PW.1 and in his chief-examination evidence he has reiterated the petition averments therein.

sentences.text: Though he has been (SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.3669/2024 elaborately cross-
examined by the respondent No.1 counsel, but nothing is brought on record to disbelieve the case of the petitioner.
On perusal of exhibited documents, Ex.P.1 is the FIR registered at Tumakuru Traffic Police against driver of the offending car.
Ex.P.2 is the Complaint which shows that, due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the car the accident took place and petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
Ex.P.3 and 4 are Spot Mahazar and Sketch showing place of accident on Gedhlahalli-Kunigal Junction Ring Road, in front of Lakshmi Tiles Company and Golden Wines, Tumakuru, which is not disputed.

Ex.P.5 is IMV report shows involvement of both vehicles in the accident and damages caused to the offending car at its front side and damages caused to the petitioner's Motor Cycle at its front and rear side.
Ex.P.6 is the Wound certificate shows petitioner sustained six injuries and all the injuries are fresh and simple in nature.

Ex.P.7 is Charge sheet shows after completion of investigation, the Investigation Officer has filed Charge sheet against driver of the offending Car as A1 and against petitioner as A2,
for the offences punishable U/Sec 279, 337 of IPC and Sec 146 and 196 of IMV Act.

The Charge sheet is also filed against petitioner for not having valid policy, it cannot be said (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.3669/2024 that the accident has also occurred due to rash and negligent riding by the petitioner.
Ex . P.10
original Medical reports.
Ex.P.14 is Discharge summary shows petitioner sustained soft tissue injury.

The petitioner got examined Medical Records Officer at District Government hospital, Tumakuru, as PW.2 and he has produced Authorization letter, MLC, Case sheet and X-ray as per Ex.P.15 to 18,
wherein it is mentioned that "RTA, while riding Bike from back car hitted".
To disprove the petitioner case, the respondent No.1 did not lead evidence.

The oral and documentary evidence adduced by the petitioner clearly goes to show that, due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending Car, the accident took place and petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
11. Issue No.2:-
This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Road traffic accident.

The petitioner in his evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident he was hale and healthy and was aged about 42 years and working as licenced Surveyor in Chikkanayakanahalli Taluk and was (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.3669/2024 earning Rs.50,000/- p.m and he has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards hospitalization, transportation and for medicines and nourishment.
Due to accidental injuries, he lost his income and became permanent disabled.

12. It is duty of the petitioner to prove his age, but the petitioner has not produced birth certificate,
school records or SSLC marks card to show his exact date of birth.
However, he has produced Ex.P.11 Aadhaar card, Ex.P.12 PAN card and Ex.P.13 Driving licence.

Even though said documents are not authenticated documents for the proof of age of any person, but in the absence of any other Lakshmikantha H B vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28340567/

sentences.text: , the same can be relied upon and according to which the date of birth of the petitioner is mentioned as 05.04.1982 and the alleged accident was occurred on 28.03.2024.

Therefore,
considering the said documents, this tribunal has assessed the age of the petitioner as 42 years.

As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and others case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 41 to 45 is '14'.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Regarding avocation and income of the petitioner, he has not produced any documents or evidence.

Therefore, in the absence of satisfactory documents in proof of the income of the injured,
this tribunal has to go by the Lok-Adalath chart, according to which the notional income in relation to the accident of the year 2024 to be taken as Rs.16,500/- p.m.

Therefore, this tribunal assessed the monthly income of petitioner is at Rs.16,500/-.
14.
As per Ex.P.6 Wound certificate the petitioner has sustained only simple injuries.
Ex.P.14 Discharge summary shows petitioner took treatment as inpatient for 4 days only.
As per Ex.P.8 petitioner has incurred medical expenses of Rs.2,428/- only.

But in this case the petitioner has not examined the doctor who treated him and has not produced any disability certificate to show that he has sustained any physical or functional disability which is come in the way of his day to day life.
Absolutely there is no evidence on record to show that petitioner sustained any physical or functional disability and no evidence on record to show his age, avocation and income.

There is no evidence on record to show that petitioner sustained loss of future income and loss of income during laid up period and also there is no evidence on (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.3669/2024 record to show that petitioner requires further treatment.

Therefore, under the facts and circumstances of the case,
this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner is entitled for Global compensation of Rs.40,000/-.
15.
Accordingly I hold that, the petitioner is entitled for Global compensation of Rs.40,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
16. Regarding liability:- Despite sufficient opportunity, the respondent No.2 remained absent and was placed exparte.
On service of notice, the respondent No.1 has appeared and filed objections and contested the matter, but not lead evidence to disprove the case of the petitioner and to prove its contention.
On the date of accident policy was in force.
Hence, respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay above said compensation amount.
Respondent No.1 Insurance Company is directed to deposit above said compensation amount within two months from the date of filing of the petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.2 partly in affirmative.

: In view of reasons assigned to Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for Global compensation of Rs.40,000/- (Rupees Forty thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.1 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

On deposit of the compensation amount with interest, since the award amount is meager one, entire award amount is ordered to be released in favour of petitioner through E-payment directly to his account by obtaining his bank account details.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
